historical_references.reference: Charurani was a queen of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling around 230 CE in the Deccan region of ancient India. She is known for her extensive patronage of Buddhism and her construction of several Buddhist viharas (monasteries). One of her most notable works was the restoration of the Amaravati Stupa, which was a major Buddhist pilgrimage site.

historical_references.reference: Charurani is also mentioned in the 12th-century Jain text 'Harivamsa' as a lay follower of Jainism. She is described as a generous patron of Jain monks and a devout laywoman who observed various penances and fasts. The text records that she donated land and other resources for the construction of Jain temples and monasteries.
